report.summary: Chunk 1 of 3 of graph_delta.py: module docstring and utility functions for loading mutations, LayerDelta and DeltaResult dataclasses, and AST-based reference/literal/structure extraction functions.
risks: load_mutations | medium | Mutations imported from tools/gate_discrimination.py; if that file changes or is missing, this module will fail at runtime, not at import time. | Verify that tools/gate_discrimination.py exists and contains MUTATIONS list.

_ast_refs | low | Multiset flattening uses #i suffix; if any identifier name already contains '#', the set difference could produce false positives/negatives. | Check if any identifier in the corpus contains '#'.

_literals_by_function | low | Constant values are clipped to 80 chars; a literal longer than 80 chars will be truncated, possibly causing false negatives if the change is in the truncated part. | Verify that no mutated literal exceeds 80 characters after repr.
_module_literals | low | Same clipping issue as _literals_by_function. | Same as above.

DeltaResult.detected_leaky | medium | The property counts all layers, including non-scoring ones; if non-scoring layers are added in the future, detected_leaky may become misleading. | Review the list of layers and ensure non-scoring layers are not added inadvertently.

claims.text: An audit measured the gate's rejection rate against the three known-bad changes of a single day at 0/3.
claims.why: This claim refers to an external audit result; the chunk does not contain the audit data.

claims.text: For a candidate patch, does the DELTA IN THE GRAPH carry information about the patch that the test suite does not — available before the tests run, at negligible cost?
claims.why: This is a question posed by the module; the chunk does not contain the answer.

claims.text: 69 of the 82 completed attempts carry a diff and all 69 are state=clean
claims.why: Refers to data in runs/spine/spine.sqlite3; not in this chunk.

claims.text: a mutation that DELETES A CALL (_verify_reachable(...) -> pass) should be visible — an edge disappears;
claims.why: This is a prediction; the chunk does not contain results.

claims.text: a mutation that makes a condition vacuous (if X not in Y: -> if False:) should be visible — the identifiers X and Y leave that function's body;
a mutation that only changes a DATA LITERAL (adding 'claude_cli' to a tuple) should be INVISIBLE — no edge moves, and I expect this layer to miss it;

a mutation that inserts an early return should be INVISIBLE to a name-based view — the following statements are still lexically present, so nothing is deleted. Catching it needs control flow, which this repo does not build.

Import the corpus from tools/gate_discrimination.py rather than copying it. One corpus, one definition — a second copy would drift and then the two measurements would disagree for a bookkeeping reason.
claims.why: load_mutations imports from tools/gate_discrimination.py as stated.

claims.text: Register BEFORE exec: @dataclass resolves annotations through sys.modules[cls.__module__], so a module that is not registered yet makes every dataclass in the imported file raise on definition.
claims.why: The code registers the module in sys.modules before exec_module, exactly as described.

claims.text: code.refs.leaky is deliberately excluded: it scans raw source, so the corpus's own 'SEEDED DEFECT' comments move it for every single mutation and a verdict built on it would be a tautology.
claims.why: SCORING_LAYERS does not include 'code.refs.leaky'; it includes 'code.refs.ast', 'literals', 'structure', 'types', 'data.literals'.

claims.text: Detected means a SCORING layer moved. It does NOT mean the defect was understood — only that the graph is not blind to it.
claims.why: The property returns True if any layer in SCORING_LAYERS has moved, matching the claim.

claims.text: What the measurement would claim if comments counted. Reported so the artefact has a number instead of a footnote.
claims.why: detected_leaky returns True if any layer moved, including non-scoring ones, as described.

claims.text: Identifier references from the AST — the CLEAN arm. THE ARTEFACT THIS EXISTS TO REMOVE. The first run of this module reported 10/12 detected, and every single detection contained the tokens SEEDED and DEFECT — the marker words the corpus writes into its own replacement comments. graph.identifiers scans raw source, so comments are tokens, and the measurement was detecting the LABEL rather than the defect. That is the same self-prediction artefact eval/ceiling.py separates with its clean and leaky arms, and it is why both arms are reported here. Comments do not exist in an AST, and docstrings are skipped explicitly, so what remains is names the program actually uses.
claims.why: The function parses the AST and walks it, skipping docstrings, extracting Name and Attribute nodes, thus avoiding comments.

claims.text: MULTISET, not a set. Set semantics erase the deletion of a call that still occurs elsewhere in the same function -- and 'this function now calls _verify_reachable once instead of twice' is exactly the kind of change a seeded defect makes. Counting is independently correct, not a tune to the answer: it was wrong before the result was known.
claims.why: The function uses Counter to count occurrences, then flattens with '#i' suffix, preserving multiplicity.

claims.text: Constant VALUES per function — the layer that closes the data-only blind spot. Three of the five mutations the reference layer missed change no name at all: FREE_LANES gains 'claude_cli'; a host constant gains localhost; an argv list loses --no-textconv. A name-based view is structurally blind to every one of them, because the identifiers are identical before and after. Constants are a multiset per function, like references, so losing one of two identical flags is visible. Values are stored as repr and CLIPPED: this layer must never become a way for a secret in a literal to travel into a report.
claims.why: The function extracts constants per function using Counter, clips repr to 80 chars, and returns a dict of Counters.

claims.text: Constants at MODULE level too — FREE_LANES = (...) is a module assignment, so a function-scoped walk would never see it change.
claims.why: The function walks only top-level statements (tree.body) and extracts constants from assignments.

claims.text: All constants, function-scoped and module-scoped, as comparable keys.
claims.why: The function combines _module_literals and _literals_by_function into a set of keys.

claims.text: Statement SHAPE per function — the layer for the control-flow blind spot. The two mutations that neither references nor literals can see change only the shape of the code: one inserts an early return, the other inverts a condition. In both, the identifier multiset and the constant multiset are byte-identical before and after, because nothing is named or valued differently — only the control flow moved. So this layer records node TYPES and their nesting depth, deliberately discarding every name and every value. That makes it orthogonal to the other two by construction rather than by hope: a change that renames a variable
claims.why: The function body is cut off at the end of the chunk; the implementation is not visible.

observations.what: load_mutations registers the imported module in sys.modules before exec_module to avoid dataclass errors; the comment explains the rationale.
DeltaResult.SCORING_LAYERS is a tuple of strings; it excludes 'code.refs.leaky' as documented.
_ast_refs flattens a Counter into a set of strings with '#i' suffix; this preserves multiplicity but assumes no '#' in identifier names.
_literals_by_function and _module_literals clip constant repr to 80 characters; changes in longer literals may be missed.
_structure_by_function docstring is cut off; the implementation is not in this chunk.
